title: Classic Cheeseburger
description: A juicy American cheeseburger with a deeply browned beef patty, melted American cheese, crisp toppings, and a toasted sesame bun.
ingredients: Ketchup, yellow mustard, and mayonnaise, for serving
instructions: Divide the cold ground beef into four equal portions and shape each one gently into a patty about 3/4 inch thick. Avoid packing the meat tightly, because a loose shape helps the finished burger stay tender and juicy.

Use your thumb to press a shallow indentation into the center of each patty, then season both sides evenly with kosher salt and black pepper. Keep the patties refrigerated while the skillet or grill heats so the fat stays firm.

Heat a cast-iron skillet, griddle, or grill over medium-high heat until very hot. A properly preheated cooking surface is important because the first contact creates the browned crust that gives a classic burger much of its flavor.

Place the patties on the hot surface with a little space between them and cook without moving for about 3 to 4 minutes. Let the underside form a deep brown crust before you attempt to turn the burgers.

Flip each patty once and cook the second side for about 2 minutes, then place one slice of American cheese over every patty. Cover briefly, if possible, so the trapped heat melts the cheese evenly without overcooking the beef.

Continue cooking until the burgers reach your preferred safe doneness; for ground beef, the USDA-recommended minimum internal temperature is 160°F. Check in the center with an instant-read thermometer rather than judging only by color.

While the patties finish, spread the cut sides of the buns lightly with softened butter. Toast them cut-side down on a clean section of the griddle or in a skillet until golden, crisp at the edges, and still soft inside.

Build each burger on a toasted bottom bun with lettuce first if you want a barrier against juices, followed by the cheeseburger patty, tomato, onion, and pickle chips. Keep the toppings balanced so the burger remains easy to eat.

Add ketchup, yellow mustard, mayonnaise, or a combination of the three according to preference. Spoon sauces onto the top bun rather than directly onto the hot patty so they stay distinct instead of immediately thinning out.

Close the burgers with the top buns and serve right away while the cheese is melted and the toasted buns are warm. Pair with fries, potato wedges, coleslaw, or a simple salad for a classic American meal.
tips: Use 80/20 beef for a good balance of flavor and juiciness.
Handle the meat as little as possible when shaping patties.
Toast the buns so they resist becoming soggy.
commonMistakes: Pressing on the burger while it cooks squeezes out flavorful juices.
Flipping repeatedly can interfere with crust formation.
Starting with a cool pan makes browning slower and less effective.
substitutions: Use cheddar or pepper Jack instead of American cheese.
Use brioche or potato buns in place of sesame buns.
Swap red onion for thinly sliced white or sweet onion.
storage: Refrigerate cooked patties in a sealed container for up to 3 days.
Reheat patties gently and add fresh buns and toppings when serving.
Freeze cooked patties without toppings for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Smash Burgers
description: Thin, crisp-edged smash burgers with caramelized beef, melted cheese, tangy burger sauce, pickles, and toasted soft buns.
ingredients: Thinly sliced onion and extra pickle chips, for serving
instructions: Mix the mayonnaise, ketchup, mustard, chopped pickles, and pickle brine in a small bowl, then refrigerate the sauce while you cook. Preparing the sauce first keeps the fast-moving griddle stage focused and organized.

Divide the cold beef into eight loose balls of roughly equal size without compressing them. Keep the balls chilled until the griddle is fully heated, because cold fat and a very hot surface encourage strong browning.

Heat a cast-iron griddle or heavy skillet over high heat until a drop of water evaporates almost immediately. Lightly butter the cut sides of the potato buns and toast them until golden, then set them aside.

Place two or more beef balls on the hot surface with generous space between them. Immediately cover each ball with a small square of parchment and press down firmly with a sturdy spatula or burger press until very thin.

Remove the parchment, season the exposed surfaces with salt and pepper, and let the patties cook completely undisturbed for about 90 seconds. The edges should look dark, lacy, and crisp before you scrape underneath.

Use a sharp metal spatula to scrape firmly beneath each patty so the browned crust stays attached to the meat. Flip once, add a cheese slice to each patty, and cook the second side for roughly 30 to 60 seconds.

Stack two cheese-topped patties for each burger while they are still on the griddle, allowing the heat to fuse the layers together. Transfer the double stacks to a warm plate as soon as the cheese is soft and glossy.

Spread burger sauce across both toasted bun halves, then place a double patty stack on each bottom bun. Add thin onion and pickle chips, keeping the toppings simple so the crisp beef crust remains the main texture.

Close the burgers gently without pressing them down, because compressing the finished patties can force hot juices into the bun. Serve immediately while the edges are crisp and the cheese remains fully melted.

For food safety, cook ground beef to an internal temperature of 160°F. If your patties are extremely thin, check a representative stack promptly so you do not leave them on the griddle longer than necessary.
tips: Use a stiff metal spatula with a thin edge for clean scraping.
Smash only at the beginning of cooking, not after the crust forms.
Cook in batches if needed so the griddle stays extremely hot.
commonMistakes: Using lean beef can produce dry patties with less browning.
Smashing on a cool surface causes steaming instead of crisping.
Trying to flip before the crust forms can tear the patties.
substitutions: Use cheddar slices if you prefer a sharper cheese flavor.
Use a cast-iron skillet if you do not have a flat-top griddle.
Serve with plain mustard and pickles instead of the burger sauce.
storage: Refrigerate cooked patties for up to 3 days in a sealed container.
Reheat quickly on a hot skillet and assemble with fresh buns.
Freeze cooked patties separated by parchment for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Beef Stroganoff
description: Tender strips of beef and mushrooms in a creamy, savory stroganoff sauce served over buttery egg noodles.
ingredients: 1 1/4 lb sirloin steak, thinly sliced across the grain
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the egg noodles until just al dente according to the package directions. Drain them well, toss with a small amount of butter if desired, and keep them warm.

Pat the sliced sirloin dry and season it with about half the salt and all of the black pepper. Dry beef browns much more effectively, so remove visible surface moisture before the meat reaches the skillet.

Heat 1 tablespoon of olive oil in a wide skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Sear the beef in two batches for roughly 1 to 2 minutes per side, then transfer it to a plate before it overcooks.

Reduce the heat to medium, add the remaining oil and the butter, then add the mushrooms in an even layer. Cook until they release their moisture and develop golden-brown edges, stirring only occasionally.

Add the sliced onion and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic for about 30 seconds. Scrape up any deeply browned bits from the pan because they add concentrated savory flavor.

Sprinkle the flour over the mushroom mixture and stir continuously for about 1 minute. Slowly pour in the beef broth while stirring, then add the Worcestershire sauce and Dijon mustard and bring the sauce to a gentle simmer.

Simmer for 4 to 6 minutes until the sauce thickens enough to lightly coat the back of a spoon. Reduce the heat to low before adding dairy so the sour cream is less likely to separate or become grainy.
Place the sour cream in a small bowl and whisk in a few spoonfuls of the warm sauce to temper it. Stir the warmed sour cream mixture back into the skillet until the sauce is smooth and evenly creamy.

Return the seared beef and any collected juices to the skillet and warm for 1 to 2 minutes without boiling. Taste and adjust the salt, remembering that the broth and Worcestershire sauce both contribute seasoning.
Spoon the stroganoff over the warm egg noodles and finish with chopped parsley. Serve immediately, because the beef is most tender when it is only briefly reheated in the finished sauce.
tips: Slice the beef across the grain for tenderness.
Sear in batches to avoid steaming the meat.
Temper the sour cream and keep the sauce below a hard boil.
commonMistakes: Crowding the skillet prevents a strong sear.
Overcooking thin beef strips makes them tough.
Boiling after adding sour cream can make the sauce separate.
substitutions: Use ribeye or tenderloin instead of sirloin.
Use Greek yogurt in place of sour cream, added off heat.
Serve over mashed potatoes or rice instead of noodles.
storage: Refrigerate in a sealed container for up to 3 days.
Reheat gently over low heat so the dairy sauce stays smooth.
Freeze without sour cream for best texture, then add fresh sour cream after reheating.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Classic Beef Chili
description: A hearty American beef chili simmered with tomatoes, beans, peppers, warm spices, and rich ground beef.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) kidney beans, drained and rinsed
1 can (15 oz) pinto beans, drained and rinsed
1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
instructions: Heat a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and add the olive oil. Add the ground beef in broad pieces, let it brown before stirring, then break it into smaller crumbles as the browned surfaces develop.

Continue cooking until no pink remains, then spoon off excessive rendered fat while leaving a thin coating in the pot. Removing only the excess keeps the chili flavorful without allowing it to become greasy.
Add the diced onion and bell pepper to the beef and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the vegetables soften. Add the garlic and cook for about 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, oregano, and optional cayenne. Toast the spices with the beef and vegetables for about 1 minute so their aromas bloom in the warm fat.
Add the tomato paste and stir for another minute until it darkens slightly and coats the meat. This brief caramelization takes away the raw tomato-paste taste and builds a deeper base for the chili.

Pour in the crushed tomatoes, diced tomatoes, and beef broth while scraping the bottom of the pot. Add the salt and black pepper, then bring the mixture to a gentle simmer rather than a vigorous boil.
Reduce the heat to low, partially cover the pot, and simmer for 30 minutes. Stir every 8 to 10 minutes so the thickening tomato mixture does not catch on the bottom as moisture slowly evaporates.
Stir in the kidney beans and pinto beans, then continue simmering uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes. This final stage warms the beans while allowing the chili to thicken to a spoonable consistency.

Taste the chili and adjust salt, black pepper, chili powder, or cayenne as needed. If it becomes thicker than you like, add a small splash of broth; if it is thin, simmer uncovered for several more minutes.
Rest the chili off the heat for 5 to 10 minutes before serving. Offer shredded cheese, diced onion, sour cream, scallions, or cornbread alongside so each person can finish the bowl to taste.
tips: Brown the beef before breaking it into very fine crumbles.
Toast the spices briefly for fuller flavor.
Chili often tastes even better after resting or reheating the next day.
commonMistakes: Boiling aggressively can make the bottom scorch as the chili thickens.
Adding beans too early can make them overly soft.
Skipping the final seasoning check can leave a large pot underseasoned.
substitutions: Use black beans in place of one can of beans.
Use fire-roasted diced tomatoes for extra smoky flavor.
Replace part of the beef with ground turkey if desired.
storage: Refrigerate for up to 4 days in a sealed container.
Reheat on the stovetop over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally.
Freeze cooled chili for up to 3 months and thaw overnight before reheating.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Chili Mac
description: A cozy one-pot chili mac with seasoned ground beef, tomatoes, beans, tender macaroni, and melted cheddar cheese.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) kidney beans, drained and rinsed
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and brown it thoroughly, breaking it into bite-size crumbles while allowing some pieces to develop darker edges.
Drain off excessive fat if necessary, then add the diced onion and cook for about 4 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic and cook for another 30 seconds, keeping it moving so it does not burn.

Add the chili powder, cumin, and smoked paprika, stirring for about 1 minute to coat the beef evenly. Stir in the tomato paste and cook until it deepens slightly in color and smells rich rather than raw.

Pour in the diced tomatoes and beef broth, scraping the bottom of the pan to release any browned bits. Stir in the drained kidney beans, salt, and black pepper, then bring everything to a steady simmer.
Add the dry elbow macaroni directly to the simmering liquid and stir well so no pasta sticks together. Reduce the heat to medium-low and keep the mixture at a gentle simmer instead of a hard boil.

Cook uncovered for 10 to 12 minutes, stirring every couple of minutes, until the macaroni is just tender. Add a small splash of broth or hot water if the pasta absorbs the liquid before it is fully cooked.

Once the pasta is al dente, remove the pan from the heat and taste the chili mac. Adjust the salt and spices before adding cheese, because cheddar will contribute another layer of saltiness and richness.

Stir in 1 cup of the cheddar until completely melted and distributed through the sauce. The starch from the macaroni should combine with the cheese and tomato broth to create a thick, cohesive coating.
Scatter the remaining 1/2 cup cheddar over the top, cover the pan for 2 to 3 minutes, and let the residual heat melt it. Sprinkle with sliced scallions just before serving for a fresh contrast.
Serve the chili mac hot from the pan, adding sour cream or pickled jalapeños if desired. Refrigerate leftovers promptly, because the pasta will continue absorbing sauce as the dish sits.
tips: Stir the pasta frequently enough to prevent sticking.
Keep extra broth nearby in case the macaroni needs more liquid.
Add the cheese off heat for a smoother sauce.
commonMistakes: Using a very small pot encourages uneven pasta cooking.
Boiling too hard can reduce the liquid before the macaroni softens.
Overcooking the macaroni makes leftovers especially soft.
substitutions: Use Monterey Jack or a cheddar-Jack blend.
Use black beans instead of kidney beans.
Use small shells or cavatappi with a similar cooking time.
storage: Refrigerate for 3 to 4 days in a covered container.
Reheat with a splash of broth or water to loosen the sauce.
Freeze for up to 2 months, though the pasta will be softer after thawing.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Beef Enchiladas
description: Cheesy Tex-Mex beef enchiladas filled with seasoned ground beef, rolled in corn tortillas, and baked in red enchilada sauce.
ingredients: 2 cups shredded cheddar or Mexican-blend cheese, divided
1 tbsp neutral oil, plus more for softening tortillas if needed
Sour cream, diced onion, and sliced jalapeños, for serving
instructions: Preheat the oven to 375°F and lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish. Spread about 1/2 cup of enchilada sauce across the bottom so the tortillas stay moist and do not stick during baking.

Heat a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the ground beef, and cook until browned. Break the meat into small crumbles while it cooks, then drain off excess fat so the filling is rich but not greasy.
Add the diced onion and cook for 4 to 5 minutes until softened, then add the garlic, cumin, chili powder, and salt. Stir for about 1 minute so the spices coat the beef and become fragrant.
Stir 1/2 cup of enchilada sauce into the beef and simmer for 2 minutes, then remove the skillet from the heat. Fold in 1/2 cup of shredded cheese and let the filling cool slightly before rolling.

Warm the corn tortillas until flexible, either in a lightly oiled skillet or wrapped in a damp towel in the microwave. Work in small batches so each tortilla stays pliable enough to roll without cracking.
Spoon a modest line of beef filling down the center of each tortilla and roll it snugly without overstuffing. Arrange the enchiladas seam-side down in the prepared baking dish in a single tight row.

Pour the remaining enchilada sauce evenly over the rolled tortillas, making sure the exposed edges receive some sauce. Sprinkle the remaining cheese across the top from edge to edge for an even baked finish.
Cover the dish loosely with foil and bake for 20 minutes, then remove the foil and bake for another 8 to 10 minutes. The sauce should bubble around the edges and the cheese should be fully melted.

Let the enchiladas rest for 8 minutes before serving so the filling settles and the tortillas are easier to lift intact. Sprinkle with chopped cilantro after baking rather than before so it stays bright and fresh.
Serve with sour cream, diced onion, jalapeños, Mexican rice, or beans as desired. Refrigerate any leftovers once cooled, and reheat covered so the tortillas remain tender instead of drying out.
tips: Warm corn tortillas before rolling to prevent cracking.
Do not overfill the tortillas.
Use enough sauce to keep the tortillas moist through baking.
commonMistakes: Cold tortillas often split during assembly.
Too much filling makes the enchiladas difficult to roll and serve.
Baking uncovered for the entire time can dry the tortilla edges.
substitutions: Use flour tortillas if preferred, though the texture will differ.
Use Monterey Jack in place of cheddar.
Add drained black beans to stretch the beef filling.
storage: Refrigerate covered for 3 to 4 days.
Reheat covered in a 350°F oven until hot throughout.
Freeze assembled enchiladas for up to 2 months and thaw overnight before baking.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Beef Burritos
description: Big, satisfying beef burritos packed with seasoned ground beef, rice, beans, cheese, salsa, and fresh toppings.
ingredients: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and rinsed
1 1/2 cups shredded cheddar or Monterey Jack
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and add the ground beef. Cook until deeply browned, breaking the meat into small crumbles and allowing excess moisture to evaporate before seasoning.
Add the diced onion and cook for about 4 minutes until softened, then stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, and salt. Cook the spices for 30 to 60 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the water and scrape up any browned bits from the skillet, then simmer for 2 to 3 minutes until the liquid is mostly absorbed. Remove the beef from the heat and keep it warm for assembly.

Warm the cooked rice and black beans separately so the burrito filling is hot throughout. Taste both components for seasoning before assembly, because bland rice or beans can mute the flavor of the entire burrito.

Warm each flour tortilla for 15 to 20 seconds in a dry skillet or briefly in the microwave under a damp towel. A warm tortilla stretches more easily and is less likely to tear when folded around a generous filling.

Lay one tortilla on a clean surface and arrange rice, beans, seasoned beef, cheese, and salsa in a compact horizontal line just below the center. Leave a clear border on both sides so the tortilla can close securely.

Fold the left and right sides inward over the filling, then lift the bottom edge up and over the ingredients. Roll tightly away from you while keeping the sides tucked in to form a neat, sealed burrito.

If you want a crisp exterior, place the rolled burrito seam-side down in a dry skillet over medium heat. Toast for 1 to 2 minutes per side until lightly golden, taking care not to scorch the tortilla.

Serve the hot burritos with lettuce, diced tomato, and sour cream either inside or alongside. Keeping watery fresh toppings outside until serving helps prevent the tortillas from becoming soggy during holding.
For meal prep, cool the beef, rice, and beans before rolling and omit lettuce, tomato, and sour cream. Wrap each burrito tightly and refrigerate or freeze, then add fresh toppings after reheating.
tips: Warm tortillas before folding.
Keep the filling in a compact line instead of spreading it edge to edge.
Drain salsa well if it is very watery.
commonMistakes: Overfilling is the most common cause of torn burritos.
Cold tortillas crack more easily.
Adding wet lettuce and tomato before long storage makes the tortilla soggy.
substitutions: Use pinto beans instead of black beans.
Use Spanish-style rice or plain white rice.
Use pepper Jack cheese for more heat.
storage: Refrigerate assembled burritos without fresh toppings for up to 3 days.
Reheat until hot throughout before adding fresh garnishes.
Freeze individually wrapped burritos for up to 2 months.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Beef Fajitas
description: Sizzling beef fajitas with marinated steak, charred peppers and onions, warm tortillas, lime, and classic Tex-Mex toppings.
ingredients: Chopped cilantro, salsa, sour cream, and avocado, for serving
instructions: Whisk 2 tablespoons of olive oil with the lime juice, garlic, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika, salt, and black pepper. Place the steak in the marinade and turn it until every surface is evenly coated.

Marinate the steak in the refrigerator for 30 minutes to 2 hours, then remove it about 15 minutes before cooking. Avoid an excessively long acidic marinade because lime juice can eventually make the surface texture soft.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet over high heat until very hot. Remove the steak from the marinade, let excess liquid drip away, and pat the surface lightly so it can sear instead of steaming.

Add the steak to the hot skillet and cook without moving until a dark crust forms, then flip once. Cook to your preferred doneness and transfer the steak to a cutting board to rest for at least 8 minutes.

Add the remaining tablespoon of oil to the same skillet, followed by the sliced bell peppers and onion. Cook over high heat for 5 to 7 minutes, tossing occasionally, until tender-crisp with charred edges.
While the vegetables cook, warm the flour tortillas in a dry skillet or wrapped in foil in a low oven. Keep them covered after heating so they remain soft and flexible when the fajitas are assembled.

Slice the rested steak very thinly across the grain, holding your knife at a slight angle for wider slices. Cutting across the muscle fibers shortens them and makes even a flavorful skirt or flank steak easier to chew.

Return the sliced beef and any resting juices to the skillet with the peppers and onion for no more than 30 seconds. Toss quickly so everything is hot while avoiding enough extra cooking to toughen the steak.

Squeeze a little fresh lime over the sizzling mixture and scatter with chopped cilantro. Taste one piece of steak with a vegetable and adjust salt only if needed, because the marinade already contains seasoning.

Serve immediately with the warm tortillas and toppings such as salsa, sour cream, avocado, or extra lime. Let each person assemble their own fajitas so the tortillas do not sit filled long enough to become soggy.
tips: Use a very hot cast-iron pan for strong searing.
Rest the steak before slicing.
Always slice flank or skirt steak across the grain.
commonMistakes: Cooking wet steak prevents a good crust.
Overcrowding the skillet steams the peppers and onions.
Slicing with the grain makes the steak seem tougher.
substitutions: Use sirloin steak if flank or skirt steak is unavailable.
Use corn tortillas for a different texture.
Add sliced poblano pepper for a deeper pepper flavor.
storage: Refrigerate beef and vegetables together for up to 3 days.
Store tortillas and fresh toppings separately.
Reheat the filling quickly in a hot skillet to avoid overcooking the steak.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: Philly Cheesesteak
description: A classic-style Philly cheesesteak with thinly sliced ribeye, caramelized onions, melted provolone, and a toasted hoagie roll.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb ribeye steak, partially frozen for slicing
Optional: sliced hot or sweet peppers, for serving
instructions: Place the ribeye in the freezer for about 30 minutes if it is not already very cold. The meat should become firm but not frozen solid, making it much easier to cut into the paper-thin slices a cheesesteak needs.

Slice the beef very thinly across the grain with a sharp knife, then separate the slices so they cook evenly. Pat away excess moisture and season lightly with black pepper, reserving most of the salt until the griddle stage.

Heat a large griddle or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat and add the oil. Add the sliced onion with a small pinch of salt and cook for 7 to 9 minutes until soft, browned at the edges, and lightly caramelized.

Push the onions to one side of the griddle or transfer them to a plate, then raise the heat to high. Spread the sliced ribeye across the hot surface in a thin layer so it sears quickly instead of steaming.

Let the beef brown briefly before turning and chopping it into bite-size strips with the edge of a metal spatula. Season with the remaining salt and continue cooking only until the meat loses its raw color.
Mix the caramelized onions into the beef and divide the mixture into four long portions shaped to match the hoagie rolls. Lay two slices of provolone over each portion and reduce the heat slightly.

Cover the cheesesteak portions for about 30 to 60 seconds so the cheese melts into the meat. Avoid leaving the thin beef on the heat for several extra minutes, because ribeye can become dry despite its marbling.

Split the hoagie rolls without cutting completely through the hinge and spread the inside lightly with butter. Toast the cut sides on a clean part of the griddle until warm and just golden around the edges.

Slide a spatula underneath one cheesy beef portion and transfer it directly into a toasted roll, keeping the melted cheese on top. Add optional hot or sweet peppers only after the core sandwich is assembled.

Serve the cheesesteaks immediately while the beef is juicy, the provolone is melted, and the rolls are warm. Wrap briefly in parchment if desired, but do not hold them too long because trapped steam softens the bread.
tips: Partially freeze ribeye for cleaner thin slicing.
Cook the beef quickly on a very hot surface.
Choose sturdy but soft hoagie rolls that can hold the juices.
commonMistakes: Thick beef slices change the texture of the sandwich.
Crowding a small pan causes the meat to steam.
Overcooking the ribeye makes the filling dry.
substitutions: Use shaved sirloin if ribeye is unavailable.
Use white American cheese in place of provolone.
Add sautéed mushrooms or peppers if you enjoy a nontraditional variation.
storage: Refrigerate cooked beef and onions for up to 3 days.
Store rolls separately so they do not become soggy.
Reheat the filling quickly on a skillet and melt fresh cheese over it.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura

title: French Dip Sandwiches
description: Warm French dip sandwiches layered with tender roast beef and provolone on toasted rolls, served with rich beef au jus for dipping.
ingredients: 1 1/2 lb thinly sliced cooked roast beef
4 sturdy French rolls or hoagie rolls
instructions: Melt 1 tablespoon of butter in a saucepan over medium heat and add the sliced onion. Cook for 7 to 8 minutes until soft and lightly browned, stirring often so the edges caramelize without scorching.

Add the minced garlic and cook for about 30 seconds, then pour in the beef broth. Stir in the Worcestershire sauce, soy sauce, thyme, black pepper, and optional Dijon mustard until the seasonings are evenly dispersed.

Bring the broth to a gentle simmer and cook for 10 minutes so the onion and seasonings flavor the liquid. Taste before adding any salt, because beef broth, Worcestershire sauce, and soy sauce can already be quite salty.

Lower the heat so the broth is steaming but not rapidly boiling, then add the sliced roast beef in small batches. Warm the meat for 1 to 2 minutes only; prolonged simmering can make thin roast beef dry and tough.

Use tongs to transfer the warmed beef to a plate while leaving the seasoned broth in the saucepan. Strain the broth if you want a clear au jus, or leave the softened onions in for a more rustic dipping sauce.

Split the rolls lengthwise while keeping a hinge if possible and spread the cut sides with the remaining butter. Toast them under a broiler or in a skillet until lightly golden, watching closely because bread can brown quickly.

Divide the warm roast beef evenly among the bottom halves of the toasted rolls, arranging the slices loosely rather than compressing them. Spoon a few softened onions from the broth over the beef if desired.

Lay two slices of provolone over each sandwich and place the open sandwiches under a broiler for 30 to 60 seconds. Remove them as soon as the cheese is melted and bubbling at the edges without burning the rolls.

Close the sandwiches and cut each one in half for easier dipping. Ladle the hot au jus into individual small bowls so every serving has enough broth without requiring people to share a single dipping container.

Serve immediately while the cheese is melted and the rolls retain some crispness. Dip briefly rather than soaking the sandwich for a long time, which gives the classic juicy bite without causing the bread to fall apart.
tips: Warm the roast beef gently rather than boiling it.
Use low-sodium broth so the au jus can be seasoned to taste.
Toast sturdy rolls to help them hold up when dipped.
commonMistakes: Boiling thin roast beef makes it tough.
Salting before tasting the concentrated broth can make the jus overly salty.
Very soft sandwich bread can disintegrate in the dipping broth.
substitutions: Use Swiss cheese instead of provolone.
Use leftover homemade roast beef in place of deli-style slices.
Add sautéed mushrooms to the au jus for a variation.
storage: Refrigerate the beef and au jus together for up to 3 days.
Store bread and cheese separately from the broth.
Reheat the beef gently in the au jus and assemble sandwiches fresh.
author: Thejan Mahakumbura
